summary: Preserve the TypeError for a derived constructor that explicitly returns a primitive other than undefined.

target.notes: After evaluating the return expression, reject non-object, non-undefined values with JavaScript TypeError; undefined means return the initialized this binding.

caveats: Base constructors treat primitive returns differently: primitive returns are ignored there.

tests.name: number return throws
tests.input: class B {} class D extends B { constructor(){ super(); return 1; } } new D();

tests.name: edge: undefined return succeeds
tests.input: class B {} class D extends B { constructor(){ super(); return undefined; } } console.log(new D() instanceof D);
